# Build, advise, teach.

::: {.lede .muted}
Sisyphe is small on purpose. One senior engineer, with trusted collaborators when the work needs them, on problems where the model has to meet a real instrument, a real robot, a real signal or a real collection. If you are not sure your problem fits, write anyway.
:::

<div class="chips"><span class="chip perceive">perceive</span><span class="chip reason">reason</span><span class="chip act">act</span></div>
<p class="outcome">You get an agent that can operate your whole application, and an evaluation that tells you when its coverage slips.</p>
<p>MCP servers and tool design for DAWs, plug-ins, creative apps and collections. We decide what the model should see, build the bridge into your object model or archive, and write the evaluation that tells you when coverage slips.</p>
<ul class="proof"><li><a href="sideman.html">Sideman</a>: 922 reachable members of Live measured against a running instance, with change observers nothing else in the field has.</li><li>Persona: real-time conversational voice pipelines, as an embedded ML engineer.</li></ul>

<div class="eyebrow field">Audio and speech</div>
### Speech, audio and music ML
<div class="chips"><span class="chip perceive">perceive</span><span class="chip reason">reason</span></div>
<p class="outcome">You get speech and audio models that hold up in production, not only on a benchmark.</p>
<p>Speech recognition and synthesis, speaker recognition, music source separation, audio classification and the language models around them. Data pipelines, training, evaluation, and getting a model into a product people use without noticing it.</p>
<ul class="proof"><li>Cisco, after acquiring Voicea: multilingual ASR and Cisco's first speaker-diarization system, shipped to millions of Webex users.</li><li>US patent on privacy-preserving speech recognition with federated learning.</li><li>Earlier, speech and speaker recognition at Ava and Voicea.</li><li><a href="https://slegroux.github.io/nimrod">Nimrod</a>: an open-source toolkit for speech, audio and language modelling.</li></ul>
</div>
:::

### Interactive systems for art and performance
<div class="chips"><span class="chip perceive">perceive</span><span class="chip act">act</span></div>
<p class="outcome">You get a real-time system that answers people, sensors or signals, with a mapping you can defend.</p>
<p>Real-time composition, sound and visual systems that respond to sensors, biosignals, movement or game state: installations, performances, museum and gallery prototypes. Psychoacoustics and emotion research underneath, so the mapping from signal to output is defensible rather than decorative.</p>
<ul class="proof"><li>The Brain Orchestra, XIM and the Sónar Robot Arena: see <a href="about.html#background">the background</a>.</li></ul>
</div>

<div class="eyebrow field">Robotics</div>
### Robotics, simulation and learned policies
<div class="chips"><span class="chip perceive">perceive</span><span class="chip act">act</span></div>
<p class="outcome">You get a simulator and training loop you can trust, and an honest answer on whether the policy learned the task or the simulator.</p>
<p>Simulators that are fast, inspectable and scriptable; reinforcement learning and vision-language-action policies; and the sim-to-real gap between them. We build the environment, the training loop and the evaluation that tells you whether the policy learned the task or the simulator.</p>
<ul class="proof"><li><a href="projects.html">Bestiary</a>: a MuJoCo quadrotor that speaks MAVLink, so Udacity course flight scripts connect unchanged, at 30 to 60 times real time.</li><li>A personal sim-to-real project on NVIDIA Cosmos.</li><li>Since 2025 the day job is vision-language-action training pipelines. That work is not for hire.</li></ul>
</div>

### Research to product, fractional CTO, scientific advice
<div class="chips"><span class="chip reason">reason</span></div>
<p class="outcome">You get a senior second opinion, or your prototype turned into software, before you commit a team to it.</p>
<p>You have a paper, a lab prototype or a data set that needs to become software, or a team that needs a senior second opinion. We read the paper, talk to the scientists and ship the code, or sit beside your team as a fractional CTO or scientific advisor. A decade in research labs, a decade in industry.</p>
<ul class="proof"><li>Tamada: fractional CTO for AI-augmented art curation, visual search over a collection from prototype to product with a team.</li><li>Parts Order: scientific advisor on music source separation.</li><li>Museaic Labs: an emotion-driven music recommendation system.</li><li>Technology transfer on interactive systems for autism with Fundación Orange and Universitat de València.</li></ul>
</div>

## How it works

::: {.steps}
::: {.step}
<div class="n">1</div>
### A written brief
Half a page: what you are building, where it is stuck, what a demo would need to show. We reply with a scope, a number of weeks and a price.
:::
::: {.step}
<div class="n">2</div>
### Two to eight weeks
A fixed engagement with a clear question. Working code in your repo from the first week, a check-in each week, and no open-ended retainers.
:::
::: {.step}
<div class="n">3</div>
### A demo, then a decision
It ends with the thing running in front of you and a written account of what worked and what did not. You decide what happens next.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
**Advisory** is the other shape: a few hours a month to review architecture, models or an agent design before you commit a team to it. **Open source first:** if the work belongs in Sideman or a public library, we will say so and price it accordingly.
:::

::: {.cta}
## Start a conversation {#contact}

Write with what you are building and where it is stuck. You will get a reply from the person who would do the work.

<a class="btn-accent" href="mailto:sylvain.legroux@gmail.com?subject=Working%20with%20Sisyphe">Write to us</a>
:::
